messages.subject: THE REJECTION RATE
parts:
Hi everyone,
I've a question again :)
I use simulate data for my research. I do that by simulateData() in lavaan.
model<-'
Ksi1=~0.5*x1+0.6*x2+0.7*x3
Eta1=~0.5*y1+0.6*y2+0.7*y3
Eta2=~0.5*y4+0.6*y5+0.7*y6

Eta1~0.5*Eta2+0.4*Ksi1
Eta2~0.7*Ksi1

Ksi1~~1*Ksi1
Eta1~~1*Eta1
Eta2~~1*Eta2

x1~~0.75*x1
x2~~0.64*x2
x3~~0.51*x3
y1~~0.75*y1
y2~~0.64*y2
y3~~0.51*y3
y4~~0.75*y4
y5~~0.64*y5
y6~~0.51*y6
'

data.sim1<-simulateData(model, sample.nobs=100L,skewness=3, kurtosis=7)

analysismodel<-'
Ksi1=~1*x1+x2+x3
Eta1=~1*y1+y2+y3
Eta2=~1*y4+y5+y6

Eta1~Eta2+Ksi1
Eta2~Ksi1

Ksi1~~Ksi1
Eta1~~Eta1
Eta2~~Eta2

x1~~x1
x2~~x2
x3~~x3
y1~~y1
y2~~y2
y3~~y3
y4~~y4
y5~~y5
y6~~y6
'
fit<-lavaan(analysismodel, data=data.sim1,int.ov.free=TRUE, estimator="MLM")

mdat <- matrix(0,100,2)
mdat[,1]<-fitMeasures(fit1,fit.measures = c("chisq"))
mdat[,2]<-fitMeasures(fit1,fit.measures = c("pvalue"))

when we simulate data,  we'll get different dataset each time we run function data.sim1.
but, I want record the result of the random data in mdat,
I mean, I hope I can run it 100 times, so that I'll fit the 100 random datasets, and I'll get 100 chi square and p-value.
My goal is to find the rejection rate of the estimator and also get the best value of the observed chisq
can lavaan do this?or is there another way to find that out?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: THE REJECTION RATE
parts: when we simulate data,  we'll get different dataset each time we run function data.sim1.
data.sim1 in your code is not a function.  It is the output returned from the simulateData() function.

but, I want record the result of the random data in mdat,
I mean, I hope I can run it 100 times, so that I'll fit the 100 random datasets, and I'll get 100 chi square and p-value.

You can write a function to do everything in your code, and then apply that function several (e.g., 100) times.  In the attached code, I simply wrapped up your syntax into a function called "runOnce", and save the results from 5 runs to test it.  Depending on how you intend to use it, you might find it helpful to break the different steps into different functions, in case you want to apply different models to the same data.  The attached code also contains functions "makeData" and "fitModel" to do the same task in separate steps.  It might also be useful to add more arguments to the functions in case you need to manipulate conditions in your simulation.  Here is a link to get you started on custom functions and using apply/lapply/sapply:

http://www.r-bloggers.com/using-apply-sapply-lapply-in-r/

Terry

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: THE REJECTION RATE
parts: when we run fitMeasures(fit, fit.measures = c("chisq", "pvalue") either use ML or MLM, it'll bring up chisq and p-value of ML, how if I want to bring up chisq and p-value of robust?

The robust values (MLM or MLR) have ".scaled" as a suffix for any measure that is affected by the change in chi-squared (i.e., also the RMSEA, CFI and other incremental fit indices).  If you want both for comparison, you can get both the uncorrected and corrected in the same call.

fitMeasures(fit, fit.measures = c("chisq", "pvalue", "chisq.scaled", "pvalue.scaled"))

On 06/07/2014 02:25 AM, andina almira wrote:
> about MLM and MLR
> In my knowledge the differences between them is lay on se (robust and
> robust.mlr) and chisq test (SB-YB), but which one better for the
> non-normal dataset?

For complete data, they are asymptotically the same. In small samples,
they behave very similar.

I tend to always use MLR.
> Could you recommend any paper or report on MLR or MLM for me?

Perhaps he original paper describing the YB test:

Yuan, KH & Bentler, PM (2000). Three Likelihood-Based Methods for Mean
and Covariance Structure Analysis With Nonnormal Missing Data.
Sociological Methodology 30:167-202.

Yves.
